description:
## Adh-Dhariyat - The Scatterers

**Revealed at Mecca**

**60 Verses in 3 Sections**

## Sections Of Surah Adh-Dhariyat

1. Judgement a surety.

2. A son prophesied to Abraham.

3. Men and Jinn created only to serve God.

## Important Topics

1. The vowful assurance of the coming of the Day of the Final Judgment (Verse 1-6)

2. The blissful life that awaits the pious ones (Verse 15)

3. The qualities of the pious ones (Verses 17-19)

4. In the earth and in the souls of the people themselves, are signs for the people who can earn the conviction from them (Verses 20, 21)

5. The angelic visitors to Abraham (Verses 24-27)

6. The tidings to the wife of Abraham, of a son in her inconceivable advanced age (Verses 29-30)

7. To continue warning, for warning certainly profits the believers (Verse 55)

8. Men and the jinn were not created but to obey the Lord (Verse 56)

## Adh-Dhariyat Section 1 – Judgement A Surety

- The Day of Judgment shall come
- When the good shall be rewarded and the evil shall be punished

In the name of God the Beneficent the Merciful

## Adh-Dhariyat Section 2: A Son Prophesied To Abraham

- The Visitors To Abraham
- A Son Prophesied To Abraham
- The Fate Of The People Of Lot And Noah

## Adh-Dhariyat Section 3: Men And Jinn Created Only To Serve God

- The Prophet An Open Warner
- Reminding Of The Truth, Profits The Believers
- The Human Beings And The Jinn Were Not Created But To Serve God

translations.1: By the scatterers (The winds.) that Scatter,
translations.2: Then those which bear their load, (The rain.)
translations.3: Then by those which speed (Travel or move.) lightly along,
translations.4: Then by those distribute the affair,
translations.5: Verily what ye are threatened with, is certainly true,
translations.6: And verily the Judgment shall surely come to pass.
translations.7: And by the heaven with its starry highways,
translations.8: Verily ye are in discordance in what ye say,
translations.9: He will be turned away from it who is to be turned away.
translations.10: Accursed be the conjecturers, (Those who conject (about God and godly affairs) and those who believe in the conjectures. Submerged into ignorance)
translations.11: Who in the abyss (of ignorance) are wandering (bewildered),
translations.12: Ask they: "When is the Day of Judgment?"
translations.13: On that day shall they be tried at the fire.
translations.14: (It will be said) "Taste ye (now) your trial (on the fire); This is what ye did seek to hasten on!"
translations.15: Verily the pious ones shall be in gardens and (among the) springs,
translations.16: Receiving (the enjoyment) what giveth them their Lord; Verily, they were ere that the doers of good.
translations.17: Little of the night was it that they used to sleep.
translations.18: And in the (hours) ere the dawn they prayed for forgiveness.
translations.19: And in their property was a share due to the beggar and the destitute.
translations.20: And in the earth are signs for those who are sure in faith,
translations.21: And (also) in your own selves; will ye not then see?
translations.22: And in the heaven (Refers not to the physical heavens but to the sublime regions proceeding from the Absolute in the Arc of Descent. A.P.) is your sustenance and what ye are promised with.
translations.23: And by the Lord of the heavens (Refer to note on verse on heavens.) and the earth! verily It (the Qur'an) is certainly the truth, just as ye speak,
translations.24: Has there come unto thee [O Muhammad] the story of Abraham's honoured guests (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "11:69"]}> - <{["Q", "11:83"]}>.) ?
translations.25: When entered they (The Angels.) upon him said they: 'Peace!'. 'Peace! Said he [and deemed] A strange people [these are] (Compare with Gen 18/1-7 and 18/10-12.) '
translations.26: Then turned he aside unto his family, and brought a fat (roasted) calf
translations.27: And set it near them (The Angels.) . He said: 'What! Eat ye not?'
translations.28: And he conceived of them a fear; Said they: "Fear thou not (Don't be surprised.) !" and gave they the glad tidings unto him of a son blessed with knowledge
translations.29: Then came forward his wife in grief, she smote her face and said she (what! I) an old barren woman (Clearly indicates that the birth of the son Isaac was miraculous to prove the Omnipotence of God to affect issues from barren women &. even virgins, if He wills.) ?
translations.30: Said they: "Thus sayeth thy Lord: 'Verily He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing'"
translations.31: He (Abraham) said "What then is your errand, O' ye Messengers (The Angels.) ?"
translations.32: Said they: 'We are sent unto a criminal people'
translations.33: That We may send down upon them (The people of Lut, Sodom and Gomorrah.) stones of clay" (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "7:84"]}>; <{["Q", "11:82"]}>.)
translations.34: Marked out from unto thy Lord for the guilty ones of excesses (Refer to Verses 11:813; <{["Q", "11:84"]}>.)
translations.35: And We brought forth (those) who were there in (the town) of the believers
translations.36: But We found not there in (the town) save one house of the Muslims (Those who submit themselves to God) " (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "11:81"]}>.)"
translations.37: And left We therein a sign (Portent.) for those who dread the painful chastisement (In the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah.)
translations.38: And in Moses, when We sent him unto Pharaoh with manifest authority (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "44:17"]}> - <{["Q", "44:31"]}>.)
translations.39: But (Pharaoh) turned away with his forces (Might hosts.) and said (pointing to Moses): '(This is) a sorcerer or a madman'
translations.40: So, We seized him and his hosts and We cast them into the sea, for he was reprobate
translations.41: And in 'Ad: when sent We upon them the desolating (Unproductive, futile.) (blast of violent') wind (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "46:21"]}> - <{["Q", "46:26"]}>.)
translations.42: It left not aught upon which it came, but turned it like (rotten) dust
translations.43: And in Thamood: when it was said unto them; "Avail ye your- selves for a while (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "7:73"]}> - <{["Q", "7:79"]}>; <{["Q", "11:65"]}>.)"
translations.44: But rebelled they against the command of their Lord, so seized them the rumbling, while they were yet looking on (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "7:70"]}>; <{["Q", "11:67"]}>.)
translations.45: Then they could not even rise (on their feet), nor could they help themselves
translations.46: And the people of Noah before (that)', Verily they were wicked people
translations.47: And the heaven, We did raise it up with (Our) Might, and verily We are the expanders (of it) expanse (This indicates the expandability of the Space - discarding the fixity of the present limitations (AP).) ?
translations.48: And the earth, We did spread it out (like a carpet), how Excellent (are We) the Spreaders (thereof)? (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "2:22"]}>.)
translations.49: And of everything have We created in pairs, that ye may reflect (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "36:36"]}>.) ?
translations.50: So fly (Seek refuge, Turn to.) ye unto God! Verily I am unto you a plain (Open.) Warner
translations.51: Set ye not with God any other god; Verily I am unto you a plain (Open.) Warner
translations.52: Even so there came not unto those before them an apostle but said they (of him): 'A sorcerer or a mad man' (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "38:4"]}>; <{["Q", "44:14"]}> and <{["Q", "51:39"]}>.)
translations.53: Have they charged this unto one another? Nay! they are rebellious (Inordinate transgressors of the law – applicable also to those who break the Islamic Laws.) people
translations.54: Then turn thou thy back upon them for thou art not to be blamed
translations.55: And remind thou, for verily reminding profiteth the believers (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "21:16"]}>; <{["Q", "38:27"]}>; <{["Q", "67:2"]}>.)
translations.56: And created not I, the Jinn and the humans, but that they may worship (To live in submission to the Lord.) (Me)
translations.57: I desire (Demand.) not from them any sustenance, nor do I desire that they should feed Me
translations.58: Verily, God He (alone) is the Bestower of sustenance, the Lord of the unbreakable strength
translations.59: So, verily those who are unjust shall have a share (of the burden) like unto the share (of the burden) which had their fellows (of old), Therefore, let them ask Me not to hasten it on (Those who do not comply to the requirement of perfect obedience.)
translations.60: Therefore, Woe unto those who disbelieve because of their day which they are promised!

exegesis.1:
As in the case of Chapter 37 this Chapter also starts with a swearing in the name of the things or the energies of nature, discharging different functions in the working of the universe - mentioned in Verses <{["Q", "51:1"]}> - <{["Q", "51:4"]}>.

It is said that once the First Holy Imam 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib was asked while he was delivering a sermon from the pulpit, by a critic (a Kharaji) _What is 'Zarriat'?_ He said, _'the winds' - What is the 'Hamilat'?_ He said, _'the Clouds'_ carrying rain - _What is the 'Jariat' that travel easily?_ He said, _the ships_ - and what is _'Muqassimat?'_ He said, _the angels_. But 'Ali's interpretation is to be taken as the simplest example of this phenomena in the Universe - otherwise the same term applies to the scattering state of matter in elementary and the nebular form which is always followed by carrying weight and the energy - which are followed in the formation of heavenly bodies travelling easily in their orbits,<{["F", 1]}> and then these carriers of loads and energies are controlled and administered by the various distributing agencies which include the heavenly bodies which distribute and regulate energies to their satellites and even the microscopic corpuscles in the blood of an earthly being distributing the sustenance of them. Thus, drawing of man's attention to these phenomena which are the clearest evidence of a design and a process, asserts what is said in verse <{["Q", "51:5"]}> and <{["Q", "51:6"]}>. (A.P.)
exegesis.5: The promise that death is not the end of the life. There is Resurrection on the Day of the Final Judgment with mercy and forgiveness to the penitent and justice and punishment to the rebellious - with an eternal life of bliss for the righteous and similarly everlasting punishment to the disbelievers and the wicked.
exegesis.7:
At a time, even centuries after which, the world did not know that the earth was round, it was not a difficulty but an impossibility for any one save the All-Knowing Author of the Universe to disclose the knowledge about the ways or orbits in the heavens. Let any intelligent seeker of knowledge from the Holy Qur'an reflect on the time taken by the non-Muslim world with all their scientific efforts and exertions to enquire into the elementary phenomenon of the working of the nature in the heavens visible over our own heads. How many centuries after, we are informed by our greatest scientists about the stars in the heavens, that there are the orbit around which revolve the planets, even this our sun being the centre for the earth and the other planets to go around it.

Only a few years ago we were informed that the sun also travels on a heavenly path - and 1300 years ago the Holy Qur'an declared that the sun travels on a course toward an appointed destination.<{["F", 1]}> The sun and the moon travel swiftly on their celestial paths.<{["F", 2]}> The sun and the moon are bound by a calculation or the reckoning.<{["F", 3]}> The sun and the moon follow a prescribed way to an appointed time.<{["F", 4]}>
exegesis.8: The variance referred to, is in their false imagination about the Holy Prophet and the Holy Qur'an, some said that the Holy Prophet was sorcerer, a mad-man, one overcome by a jinn and about the Holy Qur'an they said it was an enchanting poetry, it was the collection of the stories of the ancient people borrowed from the old people. About the Resurrection they believed it to be an impossibility.
exegesis.16:
Note the qualities of the really righteous and the pious ones. These and the many other qualities of superb excellence in the maximum degree possible, could be found in the holy Ahl Al-Bayt, in view of which we are asked to follow them, holding them as our guides and not the others with no such qualities or with defective character and conduct. It was for our own benefit that it was commanded by the Holy Prophet.

1. _"I leave behind me Two very important things, the Word of God (the Holy Qur'an) and my Ahl Al-Bayt. Should ye be attached to these Two, never, never shall ye get astray - Never shall these Two be separated from each other, until they meet me at 'Kawthar' (the Cistern in Paradise.")_

2. _The likeness of my Ahl Al-Bayt is that of the Ark of Noah, he who got into it, was saved and he who turned away from it, was drowned and lost."_

The difference between the wicked and the pious in recipiency of God's grace. (A.P.)
exegesis.21:
Reference to the wonderful endowment in the nature and the creation of man, the differences of sex - their mysterious attachment to each other, the mental faculties by which the human mind goes on discerning the secrets of the natural forces and invents newer and newer scientific implements for further progress in knowledge and its application.<{["F", 1]}>

Refers to the subjective and the objective phenomena giving evidence of the Truth. (A.P.)
exegesis.22: Refers to not the physical heavens but to the sublime regions proceeding from the Absolute in the Arc of Descent. (A.P.)
exegesis.23:
Truth is so doubtless as the people talk to each other with the surety of their ability to do it. Asma'yu says that once he was returning from the Mosque at Basra. He met a Bedouin Arab on the way who was a highway robber, with his sword and bow. The Arab asked Asma'yu his identity and the place he was coming from. Asma'yu said _"I come from the place where the Word of God is recited."_ The Arab asked _"What, is the Word of God such that men could recite it?"_ Asma'yu said _"Yes!" "it is so."_

The Arab said, _"Recite it!"_ Asma'yu recited this chapter (Sura Adh-Dhariyat) and when he reached the verse 22 saying, _**"In the heavens is your sustenance" (<{["Q", "51:22"]}>),**_ the Arab jumped down from his camel slew the animal and said _"help me to distribute this to the needy"_ and broke his sword into bits, buried his bow and arrows and ran away into the desert reciting the verse.

Asma'yu says that he _began condemning himself saying to himself Alas! a single recitation of the verse reformed a Bedouin Arab and I did not get myself reformed by it till now. "Asma'yu says that he did not see the Arab until after a long time when he saw him in Hajj (Pilgrimage), reduced by constant prayers and fasting to a skeleton."_ He took Asma'yu to the place of Abraham, a spot in the Mosque opposite to the Holy Ka'ba and requested the same verse to be once again recited and when it was recited he said _"Certainly did I have the promised sustenance,"_ and when the recitation reached this verse _"The Lord of the heavens and the earth"_ the Arab shouted aloud thrice, _"Who would defy such a Lord and enrage Him?"_ and breathed his last.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri says that the Holy Prophet said _"If any one of you even run away from his destined sustenance, it follows him and reaches him as death follows an individual and overtakes him."_ The First Holy Imam 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib said _"sustenance is of two kinds, the one is that which seeks you and the other which you seek. That which seeks you shall reach you and that which you seek might be granted to you and also might not be."_
exegesis.24: Refer to the commentary of Hud <{["Q", "11:69"]}> - <{["Q", "11:83"]}> and Hijr, <{["Q", "15:51"]}> - <{["Q", "15:77"]}> for prophets Ibrahim and Lut and the people of Lut.
exegesis.32: Concerning the people of Lut, see the commentary of Verses <{["Q", "7:80"]}> - <{["Q", "7:84"]}> and Hijr, <{["Q", "15:51"]}> - <{["Q", "15:77"]}>. As said in the commentary of al-'Araf, Verses <{["Q", "7:80"]}> - <{["Q", "7:84"]}>, the two angels first came to Ibrahim and informed him that they were sent to the people of Lut. They gave Ibrahim and his wife, Sarah, the glad tidings from Allah that in spite of their advanced age soon they would have a son, Is-haq, and a grandson, Yaqub, Is-haq's son.
exegesis.36: Compare with commentary of Verse <{["Q", "11:81"]}>. The wife of Lot was a faithless woman, hence a wife, unless she happens to have some blood relation with him, could never be the Ahl Al-Bayt of the man.
exegesis.38: Refer to the commentary of Sura ad-Dukhan, <{["Q", "44:17"]}> - <{["Q", "44:31"]}>; Sura al-'Araf, <{["Q", "7:104"]}> - <{["Q", "7:137"]}>; Sura Ta Ha, <{["Q", "20:9"]}> to <{["Q", "20:98"]}> and other references mentioned therein for Musa, Fir'awn and the people of Firawn.
exegesis.41: Refer to the commentary of Sura ad-Dukhan, <{["Q", "44:21"]}> - <{["Q", "44:26"]}> for the people of Ad.
exegesis.43: See commentary of Sura al-'Araf, <{["Q", "7:73"]}> - <{["Q", "7:79"]}> for the people of Thamud.
exegesis.46: Refer to the commentary of Sura al-'Araf, <{["Q", "7:59"]}> to <{["Q", "7:64"]}> for the people of Nuh.
exegesis.47: This indicates that although the frontiers of space are confined, they are not fixed. They can be expanded (A.P.).
exegesis.49: What is created is in pairs. The parity may refer to the composite nature of the created beings or the positive and the negative in phenomenon in the order of creation (A.P.).
exegesis.50: So that ye may remember that the Absolute One from all respects and aspects, is God (A.P.).
exegesis.52: The ways of evil in dealing with the messengers of Allah were similar in all ages<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.54: Verse 54 gives the impression that Allah might send a destructive visitation as manifestation of His wrath, but the next verse quells this apprehension. The guidance may be general in appearance, but it is directed towards man as an individual so that free from collective opinion or pressure, he may submit to the commands of Allah according to his ability and achieve success by following the divine plan (A.P.).
exegesis.55: This indicates that the guidance may be general in appearance but actually meant for particular persons who get benefited (A.P.).
exegesis.56:
The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq said that God did not create men but to know, mho with the proper knowledge, automatically surrenders himself to Him – and without knowledge the adoration could never, in the true sense of it, be an adoration. Besides the actual meaning of adoration, is not the performance of any rituals or only the few prescribed formal prayers recited by the mouth but the actual surrender of the ego in an individual, disciplining it, to act only in consonance with the expressed will of the Lord, through abiding with His prescribed law.

The whole life-activity of the individual, should be nothing but the fulfilment of the will of the Lord. It is best given in verse:

_**"Say my prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death (all) are for the Lord of the Worlds." (<{["Q", "6:162"]}>).**_

This is the object of creation, in the Holy Book, to act according to the will and Command, the most perfect form of it, is the absolute submission to His will, i.e., Islam. Therefore, of the creatures, whoever is better in manifesting his will and His command in his life, will be closer to the object of the creation, hence nearer to Him. Therefore, the more perfect in obedience, will be the nearer to the Creator. Hence the closer to Him, will be more perfect in the order of creation (A.P.).
exegesis.57:
Providing sustenance for the creatures, is equal to feeding God Himself for the creatures, all put together, constitute one family of God's creation. Hence serving the creation is serving God.

It clears that the object of creation - worship and obedience, is of no advantage or benefit to God. On the contrary, it is in the interest of the creatures to become the manifestation, of His will and Command (A.P.).
exegesis.59:
Those who did not comply to the requirement of obedience.

'Dhanoob' literally a bucket full of water tied to the end of a rope like a tale figuratively used as the consequence of misdeeds and disobedience tied to the rope of one's life (A.P.).
